title: Multi-Container Pods & Init Containers
intro: Not every pod runs one container. Init containers run and finish before the main app starts; sidecars run alongside it for the pod's whole life.

steps.prompt: The 'web' pod actually has two containers. Check the pod for its container names, not just its status.
steps.explanation: This pod runs 'app' (the actual service) alongside a 'log-shipper' sidecar that forwards logs somewhere external — both share the same pod, network, and lifecycle.
steps.why: Plain 'kubectl get pod web' only shows READY as an aggregate count (2/2), not which containers those actually are — jsonpath is how you pull out just the container names.

steps.prompt: Get logs specifically from the 'log-shipper' sidecar, not the main app.
steps.fake_output:
2026-09-27 10:00:01 Forwarding logs to collector.internal:9200
2026-09-27 10:00:05 Shipped 42 log lines
steps.explanation: Without -c, 'kubectl logs' on a multi-container pod fails and asks you to specify one — it never guesses which container you meant.
steps.why: This is why every multi-container pod situation is different from earlier single-container tutorials — the moment there's more than one, -c stops being optional and becomes required for logs/exec both.

steps.prompt: The pod is stuck Pending, and you suspect an init container is the problem. Describe the pod to check init container status.
steps.fake_output:
Init Containers:
  wait-for-db:
    State: Running
    Ready: False
Containers:
  app:
    State: Waiting
    Reason: PodInitializing
steps.explanation: 'wait-for-db' hasn't finished, so the main containers haven't even started yet — that's exactly what init containers are for: blocking pod startup until a precondition is met.
steps.why: The main container's 'Waiting: PodInitializing' isn't the actual problem — it's a symptom. The real cause is always upstream in the Init Containers section when you see that reason.

steps.prompt: Check the 'wait-for-db' init container's own logs to see what it's actually waiting on.
steps.fake_output:
Waiting for db-service:5432...
Waiting for db-service:5432...
Waiting for db-service:5432...
steps.explanation: This confirms the init container itself is looping, waiting on the database service to become reachable — the actual root cause is upstream (the database), not this pod at all.
steps.why: Same -c flag as the sidecar step — init containers and regular containers use identical logs/exec syntax, the only difference is WHEN they run relative to the pod's main containers.
